utterances.text: Is it, therefore, fair to say the Mujahedin was fighting side by side with the other three units of the ARBiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, absolutely not, because each one tried at different times, whenever they were prevented from passing, to capture that feature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you said you had a common objective. You agreed that you had a common objective.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we had a common problem, which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was not my question. Not "problem," I said "common objective." That was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I cannot give you an answer about why there was no cooperation among the units. I wasn't the commander of any of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not asking about cooperation now. You have asked the question about cooperation and you said it was a difficult question to answer. I'm asking you about fighting side by side with one another and having your common objective.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I don't understand. There was no coordination. There was -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... coordination, sir. Please don't put words into my question. I'm talking about a common objective. And if you say you don't understand, that's fine, we'll leave it at that. Madam Vidovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, I would like to ask you this: Did the Mujahedin fight in 1992 and in the spring of 1993 with the 306th Brigade, with an objective or without an objective?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: No, never. We were never together in any single action.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, can this document be put away, and if we could look at Exhibit 291. All right. This is a summary of military information, dated -- 100, dated -- number 100, dated the 7th of August, 1993. I would like you to please look at item numbered 3 in the document. Can we scroll down the document, both in the English and the Bosnian version, so we can look at paragraph marked "3" of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, can you look at this paragraph marked "3." The document describes the visit of the Travnik liaison officer to the commander of the 306th Brigade. It's a very short paragraph. Could you please read and comment upon it, as briefly as possible.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I believe that this assessment of the liaison officer is superficial. Our relationship with the Mujahedin, all from the Command of the 306th Mountain Brigade, was hostile, simply because we tried to control any kind of behaviour in our area of responsibility, and they did not agree. They did not want in any way to take into account all the legal, military regulations in respect of behaviour or conduct in our area of responsibility. They didn't take that into account at all. So I don't know if their presence would ensure safe passage. That doesn't sound credible to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm asking this now: This document bears the date 7th of August, 1993. Do you remember where the Mujahedin were billeted at that time?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: At the time, they were in a place called Poljanica [Realtime transcript read in error "Poljice"] it was a settlement close to Mehurici, where they were relocated after beginning to get into conflict with our battalion in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us where they transferred to?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: To the elementary school in Mehurici, because these were members of a battalion comprised mostly of those who were expelled or whose families were split up, and for this reason they drank a lot, they got drunk a lot, and so these incidents and the fact that the Arabs did not accept the alcohol aspect, led to them leaving the school and settling down in two abandoned houses in Poljanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you this in relation to this document, too: If you can look at the second sentence of the document, where it says -- the first sentence says: "Sepic also spoke on the subject of the Mujahedin based in the school ..." And then it says: "This grouping of the 7th Muslim Brigade." How do you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: First of all, the 7th Muslim was never in Mehurici except for individuals from the area of responsibility or the Bila Valley, who were in 7th Brigade, but evidently here the Bosniaks who were with the Arabs were often taken for some other units, to be the same as some other units, the 7th, the MOS, the Mujahedin. They were described in different ways, depending on how they were seen. A battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade was in the school only. The Arabs had two rooms which served as a storage area and offices, where they were bringing in humanitarian articles and distributing them, and they had some sort of administrative work there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It has disappeared from the screen already. On transcript page 49, lines 22, I think the witness said "Poljanica" and the transcript reflects "Poljice." I just wanted to correct that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. If I can clarify a little bit, earlier you told us of some Mujahedin staying in a school of which your brother -- your cousin was a principal in Mehurici. Am I right? You are now talking of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are now talking here of people being transferred to an elementary school in Mehurici. Are these two different schools that you're talking about, two different time places, two different organizations, or is this the same group that we talked about earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It's one school, actually, where the Mujahedin were billeted first, as I explained earlier. Then, later, we came to the same building, but a floor below. We came to the ground floor. That's where we put the 1st Battalion of our 306th Mountain Brigade. Because of their mutual quarrelling, most frequently over alcohol, but some other problems, too, these Mujahedin who were on the upper floor left the school --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Who were drinking alcohol? Your members? The Mujahedin was there on the top floor. Your brigade, is that the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They were on the bottom floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And then members of the 306th were drinking alcohol, hence quarrelling with the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Mujahedin left the school and went to stay in the village of Poljanice, but two rooms in the school they kept as a storage area, where they kept humanitarian aid which arrived and was distributed to the locals, because it wasn't safe to keep that in Poljanice. They couldn't keep it there in a secure way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's just put away the storage side. At page 50, line 1, or let me say page 49, line 25, Madam Vidovic asked you: "Can you please tell us where they transferred to?" And the answer was: "To the elementary school in Mehurici." So this is not stock being kept in Mehurici. These are people transferring to Mehurici. Which are these? Who are these people now, because the Mujahedin left and went to Poljanice. In fact, you're making this statement after you've told us that they've gone to Poljanice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I really didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me back off. You said -- let me -- Madam Vidovic said: "All right. I'm asking this now: This document bears the date 7th August 1993. Do you remember where the Mujahedin were billeted at that time?" You said: "At that time, they were in a place called Poljanice. It was a settlement close to Mehurici, where they were relocated after beginning to get into conflict with our battalion in Mehurici." That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the next question was: "Can you please tell us where they were transferred to?" And you said: "To the elementary school in Mehurici." Who are these people who are being transferred to the elementary school in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I said that, then I made a mistake. The Mujahedin, from the elementary school in Mehurici, because of conflicts with our unit that was billeted in the school, left that area and went to Poljanice. No one else came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And no Mujahedin or Arabs now remained in Mehurici school after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they just kept those two rooms where they were keeping the humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic, I think it clears the point.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I'm sorry I took your time up, but I was not following the witness. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: THE COURT: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can the witness be shown Exhibit 1137. For the record, this is the document of the 30 -- or rather of the commander of the 3rd August -- of the 28th of August, 1993, order for the resubordination of units, signed by the commander, Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, as you can see, the resubordination to the 306th Brigade of the Independent El Mudjahedin Detachment is mentioned, complete with their manpower and materiel and technical equipment. What is your comment in relation to this document, if any?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: As the document clearly says, this request had not been met.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wanted to put this on the record. The way the documents are introduced at the moment is in a summary fashion, so that my learned colleague is giving already certain content of the document. I, myself, couldn't so quickly read through the documents. I would just make a suggestion that maybe the witness gets some time to look independently at the document before its content is introduced the way it was just done. I see the answer is already on the record, but I understand my learned colleague wants to save time by this way, but I find that this is, in a way, indirectly leading also by already summarizing the content without the witness having time to look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any comment, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, Your Honour. I did the following: I indicated the date of the document, the title of the document, which indicates that this is an order for resubordination, and what I described was the first paragraph of the document. I invited the witness to comment upon the document without in any way suggesting what sort of a comment the witness is supposed to give.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just the very fact that my learned colleague has said that this is an order for resubordination to the 306th Brigade of the independent El Mudjahedin Detachment, I have to say I don't get this so quickly here from reading the first paragraph of this document. It says, at least in my translation: "The aggressor forces in the 35th Division ..." So I don't get it so quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "Aggressor forces"?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Exhibit 1137.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where is "aggressor forces"?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: That's the first paragraph here. Oh, I'm sorry, I'm obviously working from a wrong copy here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You certainly are, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are. Okay. And also remember that this is already an exhibit. There's no need to lay a foundation for it. So, okay, Madam Vidovic, your learned friend has realized his mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine, Your Honour. I also happen to make such errors.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness please comment on the document?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: The document clearly states this order was never implemented, and this was confirmed with a signature that I can decipher right now. The fact of the matter is that the El Mujahid Detachment had never, in any way, been resubordinated to or engaged in coordinated action with the 306th Mountain Brigade. That's become quite clear by now, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can put this document away now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, again the question is: If the witness testifies that the subordination never happened, and this was ordered in August 1993, which is, as I recall, shortly after the establishment of the El Mujahid Detachment, the question that springs to mind is: Why on earth didn't it happen? Now we see that the Command of the 3rd Corps is taking an active role in coordinating matters within the ambit of the corps, so one would expect that things would change now. But apparently they did not, and I would like the witness to explain to us why not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the start of the inception of the 306th Mountain Brigade, or, rather, since its inception, our relations with the detachment were quite troubled, since we wanted them to abide by all the legal, military and other regulations, which they never did. They saw us, members of the brigade command, as enemies trying to impose upon them matters that they did not wish to accept. Our relations were so poor that they did not want to go along with us. They would not have acted upon the order of the commander of the 306th Mountain Brigade. This was something that we could not work upon them to accept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But may I then ask why a matter like this was not handled and resolved by the 3rd Corps? And I suppose that in my question lies a presumption that this noncompliance with the corps' order was reported to the corps, so I should be more precise and ask you, first of all: Did you report this to the 3rd Corps Command, to Commander Hadzihasanovic, and what did he do about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Naturally, we had to submit a report. Now, why he did not take certain measures, I cannot speak on his behalf, but I suppose that he had the same reasons as we did. The 306th Mountain Brigade, although we were a strong unit, why we were unable to come into a direct conflict with them, this was because of the great support that the population, in general, gave them. And their weaponry, although fewer in quantity, was far more sophisticated. Entering into such a conflict with them would not have been wise at all under those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just for my edification, you said you can decipher the signature below the handwritten comment. Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I suppose it's the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But the commander's signature is below the order. It's a long signature. That other one is a short, small signature. And you said the document clearly states this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Commander?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me tell you what you said at page 56, line 6: "The document clearly states this order was never implemented, and this was confirmed with a signature that I can decipher right now." I thought you were talking about the signature below the comment: "Order not carried out." Are you mistaken to say you can decipher the signature? Was that a mistake, sir, or are you misinterpreted, mistranslated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The signature which was placed below the block of text saying: "Not carried out," is something that I cannot decipher, this short signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Then I suspect, then, the interpretation was -- thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Unless there are other questions related to the document, I want the document to be put away. I would like to dwell for some time on the 7th Muslim Brigade and the Mujahedin. Can the witness be shown two documents, one at a time, and I will invite the witness then to comment upon both documents at the same time, because I have my reasons for it. Can the witness now be shown Exhibit 997, please. For the record, I will state that this is an information about the factors that affect the morale within the AOR of the 306th Mountain Brigade of the 6th of July -- or, rather, the 6th of May, 1993. Can the witness be shown page 3 of the document to see where the signature is. In the English version, that's also page 3, I believe. Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, the signature is mine. I'm the author of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown page 2 of the document now. The last paragraph of the page, can the witness be shown the last paragraph of the page. That's page 3 of the English version, second and third paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you're finished with the last paragraph, Mr. Husic, can we turn to the last page, page 3 of the Bosnian version. Please look at the first paragraph. It is clear that the document speaks of the presence of a larger number of foreigners in the area and of the 7th Muslim and the 314th Brigade are mentioned, and please keep this in mind while I show you another document. And remember that the document is dated the 6th of May. Also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can, Your Honours. If it's easier, I can put my question in relation to this document right now. Otherwise, I wasn't meaning to go back to the document. But we can complete it first and then move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm asking because I would have a request for clarification of the two paragraphs that you have drawn our attention to on page 3. Now, I don't expect you to put my questions, but you could ask the witness if he could clarify a bit about, first of all, in the second paragraph, in the last line, he mentions that they had made several appeals to the command of the different Mujahedin Arab groups in Mehurici, and all of these appeals had turned out to be fruitless. I'd like to hear more about that. And, secondly, still you will recall that a number of questions had been put by the Judges this afternoon about the variety of Arab groups in Mehurici, so I wonder if you could clarify, at this time here in May, June 1993, which Arab groups were stationed in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was one group at Mehuric. There was another group at Guca Gora. In our area of responsibility, from the Zenica area a third group would oftentimes arrive, which we referred to as the unit called -- just give me a moment -- "Gerila." This was a group which we didn't know where it was stationed, but which was active within our AOR. They were known as the Abu Zubeir's group. Therefore, there were several groups of which status we were unaware. But these appeals were sent to the Command of the 306th, which wanted to, with the assistant of the superior command, introduce order in the AOR of the 306th Mountain Brigade, among all the groups moving about the area and creating problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You said that you had made appeals to them. Can you explain to us how you made appeals to them and what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whenever we received a complaint which had to do with members of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, we asked their commands to keep their members in check. Now, as for these groups of foreigners, there was no way that we could work upon them or influence them. They did not want to communicate with us, and for that reason we asked the superior command to assist us in this matter, and we, in turn, also reported to them on the problems that we were faced with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I realize the situation must have been very frustrating, but what I'm -- what I'm looking for is whether you were actually in contact with the commands of these two or three groups within your area of responsibility. Were you on talking levels to them or, you know -- how did you appeal to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, except for this group in Mehurici, none of them had a command, nor did we know who was the person in charge in these groups. I have to explain that these were what we would call "dogs of war," groupings which looted in an organised way and plundered, and any contact with them was impossible. And this is why they felt, to a large degree, that we were their enemies. And our part, we were not any more tolerant towards them, either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But let us then just have a look at the Arabs who were billeted in Mehurici. Did you just cross the bridge over the river and walk over Poljanice and ask to talk to the commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the only group that we were able to communicate with was that group in Poljanice. I did not personally go to Poljanice and communicate, but some people that they tolerated better or respected more, we would send such people to their unit; yes, that is what we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: This is exactly what I was looking for. So what happened when you sent these guys over? As I recall, the distance between Mehurici and Poljanice is very short, so they could have walked over there in ten minutes. What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, after those individuals got a promise, there were actually no changes in the behaviour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see. So you're telling us that, in fact, someone from the 306th Brigade actually did manage to talk to them and also got a promise or some sort of reassurance that now things would be better, but they never became any better; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did appeal, not only the people from the 306th Mountain Brigade, but also from the civilian structures and the clerics. People from those circles were asked to convey to them our appeals not to create problems, but we did not get explicit guarantees that they would stop or not stop doing this. But actually, in practice, nothing changed, in terms of the previous situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: May I put one last question? I hope that I'm not taking the wind out of your sails, but the question that I have is: Was the 3rd Corps ever involved in these appeals? I mean, General Hadzihasanovic was not just anybody, he was a very powerful and strong man, so did he take a part in seeking to clarify these?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From our side, this is precisely what we asked for, but there was no specific result. I don't know whether the 3rd Corps did anything at the time in relation to that unit, but I know that some other problems that had to do with the 17th [as interpreted]Muslims with the members of -- which we also had some problems, these were people from our valley who lived there, their homes, their families were there, so we did manage to resolve the problems with the members of those units. However, it was ordered that the 7th, in its direct contacts with us, should resolve those problems, and we did this very effectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just to clarify for the transcript, you mentioned the 17th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 7th.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 7th. So page 63, line 4, instead of "the 17th Muslim," it should say "the 7th Muslim Brigade." And while we're still here, and I see the document on this page, it says: "The willful behaviour of groups and the 7th Muslim Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please just give us a very brief comment on that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Individuals who belonged to the 7th, which was later confirmed by their command, then a group joined this group of Arabs who actually introduced themselves as members of the 7th Muslim Brigade. And the 7th Muslim Brigade Command, we were actually told that these were not their members, that they had become renegades a long time ago, that they didn't know where they were and where they were billeted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, if you can remember approximately when you got this information about this group representing itself as being part of the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I probably will not be able to be specific, but it was sometime in April or May 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would now briefly like the witness -- well, we can put this document away, and the witness can look at Exhibit 167. For the transcript, this is the minutes from a meeting of the Joint Command -- the Joint Operations Team meeting held on the 8th of May, 1993. This is also a document in which the 306th Brigade is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that? And I would like you to look at the end of this document. This is on page 2 in the English. Can you please look at paragraph 3. Very well. I would like to ask you this: Do you recognise the names that are mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, these are my colleagues from the 306th Mountain Brigade, Mustafa Fazlic and Omer Alihodza.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you look at paragraph 3 now? Could we zoom in on paragraph number 3, please. Could the usher enlarge that portion of the text. Witness, the document states in paragraph 3 that: "The problem of foreigners in the brigades' zones of responsibility was discussed, and it was established that they are only present in the 7th Muslim Brigade. The 3rd Corps Command was requested to either relocate them from the area of responsibility of the 306th Brigade or to place them under their command." I would like to ask you if you were aware of this situation.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the problem that we had spent a long time on, but we didn't have a solution or a way of resolving it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, foreigners in the 7th Muslim Brigade are mentioned. What is your comment about that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: First of all, the Bila Valley never had units of the 7th Muslim Brigade. No unit of the 7th Muslim Brigade was located there. What this is about is this group that I mentioned before that did not belong to the 7th Muslim Brigade but was headed by a certain person called "Ramo Durmis," and the 7th Muslim Brigade regularly informed us about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what did the 7th Muslim Brigade say about Ramo Durmis in this report?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: That a few months before that, he had left the 7th Muslim with that group, and for a long time he said in the Bila Valley that he was -- or that this was a unit of the 7th Muslim Brigade. But when this was denied by the 7th Muslim Brigade and the true situation was made known, then he joined the Mujahedin, and from then on said, about himself and his group, that they were Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this paragraph 3, it is said that the corps was asked either to relocate them or to place them under the command. Do you know if there was any reaction back from the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I'm sorry to interrupt. I know you asked the witness to comment on the statement that it was established that they are only present in the 7th Muslim Brigade, and I tried to follow the answer the witness gave. It just does not seem to address that point, and I would like to get that point addressed, because I was going to ask that question myself. You had established, sir -- this group of yours here, Mustafa Fazlic and Omer Alihodza and the rest, established that these people -- these foreigners were present only in the 7th Muslim Brigade. You were being asked to comment on that. Is it a fact that there were foreigners in the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That part that we were considering or that part about which Ramo Durmis said was the 7th Muslim, there was some foreigners in that group, and we informed the command about that. Then the 7th Command denied this, about these foreigners --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I interrupt you, sir. You see, this is precisely what is confusing me. I don't see the name "Ramo Durmis" in this page or on this paragraph, and I'm asking you a very simple question. You can answer it either by saying "yes" or "no" or, "I don't know." Did you establish, as this team here, operations team, that there were foreigners in the 7th Muslim Brigade? Don't give me a long story, one word, "yes" --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So this is not correct that is mentioned here on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot answer this question with a "yes" or "no," because that part that represented itself as being part of the 7th but was not actually a part of the 7th was considered by these people to be part of the 7th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you said this group -- I thought it was part of the 7th Muslim Brigade and that this group abandoned the brigade and established the El Mujahid Detachment, or did I misunderstand something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could you please explain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The group that left the 7th Muslim Brigade for a long time represented itself separately from the 7th as part of the 7th. And when we were informed by the 7th Muslim Brigade that they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but after -- I'd like to know exactly, but before they actually left the 7th, they were part of the 7th Brigade, weren't they? That's more clear, then, if they were. But then could you make a difference in time, in the timeline, to tell us exactly when they left the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot answer precisely, but we were informed by the command that for several months the group headed by Ramo Durmis did not belong to their unit any more because they had left it of their own will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before they left, they belonged to the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you again. When did you find out this fact that they were at one time members of the 7th and that they were now quite incorrectly saying they were still the 7th?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: After a few months, the 7th Muslim Brigade informed us in the way that the assistant commander for morale came to the 306th Mountain Brigade, he gave us a list of their members from our valley, and told us that many of those presenting themselves as members of that unit were not actually members of that unit. I cannot tell you the date, but this is maybe April or May. More likely, it would be April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you very much. Now I would like to look at this document with you. Can we please look at Exhibit 123. For the transcript, this is a document of the 7th Muslim Brigade of the 30th of May, 1993. It's a short document. I don't expect you to recognise a document of the 7th Muslim Brigade, but it's a short document. I would like you to look at it. It talks about insignia and the process of marking, which according to this document, and to gain a little bit of time, I'm going to interpret it, it says the process of marking has not even begun. And you can see this is the 30th of May, 1993. I would like to ask you the following: In that area on the 30th of May, 1993, did the units have insignia on their sleeves?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Not only did they not have insignia, they didn't even have uniforms for another two or three months after that. We didn't even have 30 per cent of the men with weapons and uniforms, never mind with insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. We can put this document away, and the witness can now please look at Exhibit 90. For the record, let me say that this is a document from the 306th Brigade, and it deals with the death of Sakib Brkic. It's the 17th of May, 1993. This document is also short. Please take a look at it. It says here: "Official note" on the death of this person, drafted on 26 May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Had you heard of the death of Sakib Brkic?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, he's a very close -- he's a neighbour. Our parents were very close friends, and this is a minor boy. His parents had allowed him to join the training, and he died, and it took about six days to remove his body from the place where he had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you please take a look at the last sentence of this document. It says there: "The group of Mujahedin was led by Ramo Durmis from Zenica, who is currently the commander of the Bosniaks among the Mujahedin in Mehurici." In relation to this, let me ask you this: At this time, when this document was drafted on the 26th of May, 1993, did you or did you not know the status of Ramo Durmis then?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the 306th Brigade, where it says that the group of Mujahedin was led by Ramo Durmis from Zenica. Was this the time -- or, rather, did you find out about Ramo Durmis before or after this document?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: We found out that Ramo Durmis had left the 7th Muslim Brigade. We knew that, but we didn't know what his relationship with the Mujahedin was. He posed as the Mujahedin, his unit as the Mujahedins. For a while, they would deny this. Occasionally, they cooperated. So their relationship remained unclear to us to the end. We took it as he represented it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The gist of my question is this: Perhaps we did not understand each other very well. Did you find out -- did you receive the information about Ramo Durmis and his membership of the 7th Brigade, find out before or after this document which bears the date 26th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, thank you. This document may not be removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Was Sakib Brkic a member of either the Mujahedin or the Frankopan Brigade? How did he die? Was he a member of any of these two groups that were fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a minor, a young boy who joined the group of Ramo Durmis for training, and as they were moving in the area of responsibility under the control of the HVO, they drew fire from them and, among other things, this young boy was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They drew fire from whom, from the Frankopan Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document may now be removed, and I would like the witness to be shown document D1032. Let's just wait for the document to be removed, the current document. Could we please go to page 11 of this document, page 11 of the original, which is in Italian, and in English it is page 1. If we can just see this blown up. Of course, the witness cannot read Italian, but we will provide for the witness a hard copy of this document. May I ask the assistance of the Court Usher. We've prepared copies of this document in the Bosnian language for both the witness and the Prosecution. This is a fax sent from Sarajevo to Sheik Shaaban. I don't expect you to identify this document. I would just like to ask you some questions about some facts that we see in this document, and I'm specifically talking about the last portion -- the last third of this document. Could we bring that up on the screens, please. But before we do that, I have this question:

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From what you have said so far, we can understand that you were in contact with the 7th Muslim Brigade to deal with the issue of rowdy behaviour of their members, the Mujahedin. What I would like to ask you is this: Did you know, in June and July of 1993, what the relationship between the foreigners and the 7th Muslim Brigade were, if you had such knowledge?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, we knew of this because, in addition to these official reports on contacts, I had a colleague within the Command of the 7th Brigade, he was a colleague from work, Mahmut Effendi Karalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm apologise, Your Honour. I have to react. I have to say for the record that I will request -- that I would request that the audiotape of today's proceedings are to be checked, because at times I can see questions that are absolutely -- do not reflect what I said. So what I would now like to ask is this: I would just like to correct the question. I never said in my question, that's line 22, that -- I said that I wanted to ask him about the conduct of the members of the 7th Muslim Brigade and of the Mujahedin, and I never said that they were, as it says here, that the Mujahedin were members of the 7th Muslim Brigade. That's what could be inferred from what it says here in the transcript. If I misunderstood this, to me it appears as if this question here suggests, as read from the transcript, that the Mujahedin were members of the 7th Brigade. What I did ask is this:

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in June and July 1993, did you know what the relationship between the Mujahedin and the members of the 7th Brigade were, if you know?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because within the Command of the 7th, I had a colleague from work, Mahmut Karalic, whom they tried to assassinate, and on this occasion several people were killed. I do not know exactly what number of people, and from then this conflict was simmering on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And just to clarify, Mr. Husic, when you say Mr. Karalic, there was an attempt on his life from them, who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: The Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you please take a look at this document, and especially the part beginning with: "Dear Sheik --" "Dear and noble sheik ... " it is 10 to 12 lines from the bottom. It says: "I would like to tell you about treason committed by the Bosnian Army. The commander of the Bosnian forces managed to kill four Mujahedin Arabs here. After this, he escaped. We tried to find him and demanded that he be tried according to the Sharia law, but they," as it says here, "refused knowing full well that he was a graduate of the Al-Azar University, an Islamic religious school from Cairo. This commander's name is Ahmed Karalic, and he is the head of two combat units in the city of Zenica." What I would like to ask you is this: You just mentioned that you knew Effendi Karalic. Was he a graduate of the Cairo University?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How would you comment, this portion of the document?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: The facts are these: Whoever tried to bring some order and orderly conduct, he would clash with these groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to ask you something else. Did this actually happen?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is about -- this is the same event that I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The name mentioned here is "Ahmed Karalic"?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: When you translated back from the Arabic, and everyone who translates knows what it's like, this is translated into B/C/S in the Latin script alphabet, and it says C-A-R-O-L-I-C, where in fact it should be "Karalic," "Ahmed Karalic."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I would like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit 1201.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I didn't quite understand who refused, because in Italian, it is in the singular, whereas here we've been told "they refused," so I'm not quite sure I understand who refused, from what you understood in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can we just clarify this question that Judge Lattanzi posed. Tell us, did you have information -- you said you knew Effendi Karalic. Did the Arabs seek for him to be handed over, and if so, who by?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. They asked from the Command of the 7th Brigade to hand him over so that they can try him according to their own rules and regulations, and the Command of the 7th refused to do this. They refused to hand over Professor Karalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it is possible that's in the singular, because in Italian the singular is being used, "he refused ," "he refused."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The brigade or the brigade command refused to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this further complicates the matter. Now we have a fourth language, an additional language. But, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned during your testimony, and I think you mentioned it at least twice today, that in the Bila River Valley, there were no units of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and I would now like to clarify this a bit. Could we please show the witness Exhibit 568 [as interpreted] Exhibit 268. Your Honour, I apologise. In the transcript, it says "568," but in fact it should be "268." Witness, this is a short document. For the record, may I say that this is a document from the 306th Brigade of the 13 May 1993, and would you please read it. It says -- it speaks of a part of the troops currently stationed in Kljaci village who are members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, that they should be attached to the unit of Kljaci village. And I would just like to hear your comment on this. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was a situation, after the blockade of the Bila River, Bila River Valley, and after it was cut off in several places, as a result of which a number of villagers from the Kljaci village who were members of the 7th Muslim Brigade found themselves stationed at their own houses, and the commander of the 306th Brigade, the 306th Mountain Brigade, asked that these members of the 7th be resubordinated to him so that they would not act on their own in our area of responsibility, which is what happened. But because at this time the 306th Brigade was also not operating within a formation, but rather each village was cut off and acting on their own, these members of the 7th Muslim Brigade were together with their people from the village of Kljaci regarding of which unit they were in, because we did not operate as a military unit but, rather, as the local population.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Whatever the case may have been, I would like to ask you this: How far was this village of Kljaci from Maline, if you know?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to be precise, but I believe some 10 to 15 kilometres. It was impossible to communicate between two villages, let alone along greater distances.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that it was impossible to communicate, what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the fact that the HVO forces had cut off internally the various parts of the Bila Valley, one from another.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Whatever the case, was this group active with the 306th in Kljaci, did it become a part of it from that point?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you know these lads? Did you see them at the time?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I knew most of them. Some of them were my schoolmates. Others were my neighbours. Han Bila and Kljaci are very close to each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they wear insignia -- or, rather, did they have long beards or did they have any other hallmarks that would indicate that they were foreigners, or were they local lads?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: No, by all the traits they were local lads who were members of the 306th, and they had more uniforms themselves, locally, than other members of the 306th Mountain Brigade at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put this document away now. Can the witness be shown D230 now. For the Registrar's benefit, let me say that this document, D230, was admitted into evidence pursuant to a decision of the Trial Chamber, dated the 5th of March, 2008, but has not been given an exhibit number yet. We wouldn't want it to receive an exhibit number twice. That's why I'm saying this. This isn't the document I was calling for. I'm calling for D230. What we're looking at is 1230. I'm referring to document 230. That's fine. Can we have the English version as well. While we're waiting for it to showup, let me state that this is an order of the 3rd Corps, dated the 3rd of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to direct your attention to the portion which states that the document was sent to the commands of the operational groups, to OG Commands, therefore. Let me ask you this: Did it so happen that the commands of the operations groups would forward documents to you?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the regular procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please turn to item 5, which states the name, the reputation and image --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. I don't understand why the witness would have received this document. As far as I have understood, he was in the 306th Brigade, and this document is addressed to the 301st 3rd and 314th Brigades, but maybe the witness can help us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 306th Mountain Brigade was resubordinated to Operations Group West, Zapad at the time, which means that it was part of the Operations Group, Zapad. It was true this Operations Group that the document we have here also relates to the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me clarifies this further.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see this document? Did I show this document to you during proofing?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at item 5 of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, which one is Operation Zapad here, or Operation Group Zapad here, or Group West, Zapad? It's operation groups commands of 301, 303, 314 Brigades, commander of Reconnaissance and Sabotage Brigade, commander of Headquarter Support Units, District Defence Staff. Which one is Operations Group Zapad of which 306th was a part?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be of assistance. Please read the first line in the heading, which says: "OG Operations Group Commands." One of the groups is OG West, the group the witness was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you have occasion to read item 5 of the document?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see the document earlier or, rather, to receive it at the time of the war?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to page 2 of the document. The same applies to the English version, or, rather, it's page 3 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, while we're waiting for the right page in the English version to appear, please look at item 16 of the document. Can we scroll the document down to see the stamp and signature. Thank you. We can see that it says: "Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic." Look at item 16. A moment ago, His Honour Judge Harhoff asked you about the reactions of the 3rd Corps to the reports you sent them. I will quote item 16 and ask you to comment upon it. It reads: "All armed formations that have not placed themselves under the command of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina are to be dealt with straight away. As for the HVO units, full cooperation should be established with them due to their being part of the regular armed forces. Instructions as to the further modes of organisation will soon follow." Please, what is your comment about this? You will recall that you received an order to sort the situation out with regard to armed formations?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not tie that up with those reports. This was the general area of the 3rd Corps Command. From the very start, we had been trying to place everything under our --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just I -- sorry to interrupt, because the witness is in the middle of answering already, but I had to listen to the translation. The question which was just put was leading again: "You will recall that you received an order to sort the situation out with regard to armed formations?" I must say this is fully leading, and I don't understand where this is coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will say it again, that it's been misinterpreted. I asked the witness, "Did you remember whether you received this order?" Your Honour, I'm sure that I didn't put the question the way it's been interpreted. I put it precisely the way I speak. I suppose Judge Lattanzi can hear the way it is interpreted in French, and I'm sure this is not the way it was put.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just the use of the language, "the order to sort the situation out with regard to armed formations," I don't see that in the wording of this document in that specific way as it is put to this witness, and I find it is leading, therefore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But your learned friend says that's not what she said, it is being misinterpreted, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm not a judge and cannot assess this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Neither can I. We're in the hands of the people who speak the language. Okay. Thanks for the explanation, Madam Vidovic. I guess you may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, do you remember, did you receive such an order with the contents that we can read in item 16 of the document from the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the 306th Brigade or not try to resolve problems with armed formations? And I'm referring only to the Mujahedin here.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I've repeated it several times already. We've been trying -- we had been trying to do that, but were unsuccessful. We weren't able to attack them, to use force, because in that case we would have come into conflict with our own population and we would have produced a second Bosnian Krajina. And we had no other ways of dealing with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, the Judges or most of us here, for that matter, fail to understand what you meant to say when you said, "We would have made a second Bosnian Krajina." Just explain briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Our units would have clashed with our population, a brother against a brother, a child against a child. We would have produced the same effect that Fikret Abdic produced in Bosnian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain the extent to which the support of the population and why was there, in fact? Was it solely the population or was there somebody else involved in this support?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Primarily, the grassroots population supported them because of the humanitarian aid they received, and there were some politicians, some members of the religious circles, and engaging in conflict with them would have meant engaging in conflict with one's own people. I can give you an illustration from my own home. My father, after I refused to join them, and went off, as he put it, with the partisans, because that's how he referred to the 306th, refused to speak to me for months after that, but he simply failed to understand the political situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it seems to me that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. But just before we remove this document, I want to clear one little point. At this time in point in the war in Bosnia, now this is around April 1993, against which army were the Bosnian Army fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Against the Serbian-Montenegrin aggressor, or the Chetniks, as we called them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'll tell you why I asked this question. I thought I got the impression, or I thought I heard you a few minutes ago talking of fighting the Croats or the HVO; and now I see this document talks of the HVO units, full cooperation should be established, and that is why I am asking this question. I may have misheard you. You have not said this afternoon, at some stage, that the HVO were your opponents? I'm not able to find it on the transcript. I would have to take time to find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you're right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. At this point in time, we were aware of the fact that Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the BH Army, if they entered into a conflict with the HVO, would not survive. We did our best to avert any such clashes. There were occasional incidents, but every time we tried to overcome them. Such were also the orders and suggestions arriving from the higher command, that we should engage in conversations and negotiations to overcome these excesses that occasionally happened and involved the HVO forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought you wanted to -- did you want to say something, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'll try and find this. Thank you very much. We will take an adjournment and reconvene tomorrow at quarter past 2.00, same court. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of March, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.
